text:
Mia L: heads up — customer on dedicated GPU pool says their outbound healthchecks to our regional LB are flapping. they have a corporate outbound proxy + allowlist. any quick checks?
Raj P: which region and what IPs are failing? do we have the customer's allowlist config?
Mia L: eu-west. they pasted logs showing TCP RST from proxy when our healthcheck hits different source IPs. they also have TLS inspection enabled.
Sara K: TLS inspect usually breaks SNI-based healthchecks. ask them to allow the LB FQDN (health.rw-inference.eu-west) and the ASN ranges, not just a single IP.
Omar S: also check ephemeral SNAT rotation — if their proxy only allows a fixed port range or per-source-port mapping, our healthchecks may appear from different ports and get dropped.
Mia L: @Raj can we publish a minimal checklist for customers with proxies/hairpinning? quick one-liner they can paste into firewall team.
Raj P: yes — short checklist: 1) allow healthcheck FQDN + resolve to IPs, 2) allow outbound ports 443/80 to our egress CIDRs, 3) exempt LB healthchecks from TLS inspect, 4) preserve source ports or allow high ephemeral port range.
InfraBot: automated note — known egress CIDR for eu-west (rotates): 34.210.128.0/20, 34.211.0.0/18, 18.198.0.0/16 (verify with control plane).
Sara K: add that we do periodic IP rotation for HA; recommend allowing DNS names or /16-ish ranges where possible.
Devex Sam: here's a paste-able firewall rule example for customers on iptables or their proxy ACLs:
```
# allow outbound to Redwood healthchecks
-A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 34.210.128.0/20 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
-A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 34.211.0.0/18 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# allow ephemeral ports back to LB (if proxy preserves source port)
-A INPUT -p tcp --sport 443 --dport 32768:65535 -j ACCEPT
```
Omar S: for customers using corporate proxies that terminate TLS, they need to whitelist the LB hostname in the proxy config or add an explicit CONNECT pass-through for the healthcheck host. otherwise SNI will be mangled.
Mia L: they also reported 502s from our side when probes started failing — could be our backend draining logic. @Raj can we add a note to prefer DNS-based healthchecks rather than hard IPs?
Raj P: yep. recommend they point ACLs at the LB FQDN and schedule periodic checks for our published CIDR changes. if they cannot, they should allow larger CIDR blocks for the region.
Sara K: troubleshooting tips to send them: 1) run `curl -v --resolve health.rw-inference.eu-west:443:34.210.128.10 https://health.rw-inference.eu-west/` to force SNI/IP mix, 2) check proxy logs for TLS inspect / HTTP CONNECT rewrite.
Mia L: gave customer the checklist + curl snippet. they replied saying their proxy vendor only allows a /24 per business unit. that's going to be painful.
Devex Sam: if they cannot expand ranges we can offer a dedicated static-egress pool for that account (extra cost + contract). @Omar we have a playbook for sales ops?
Omar S: yes, sales can route that. it's the same Dedicated static egress flow we used for Acme last quarter — needs procurement lead time.
Raj P: final note — document in onboarding: include 'allow TLS passthrough for healthcheck host' and a line about 'source-port preservation recommended'. saves a lot of back-and-forth. :thumbsup:
Mia L: thanks team. I'll close the loop with customer and open a ticket for static-egress option if they can't widen their allowlist.
InfraBot: incident-triage: ticket created RW-34567 for follow-up (assigned to Raj P).
